title: He used to be pretending to be laid up with a sick voice doing his highness to make himself interesting to that old
html_source:
A hypothetical innocent reader must be quite observant to deduce that he is Bloom from earlier references to the City Arms Hotel (Norris, M. Virgin and Veteran Readings of Ulysses, p.237).

There are no indications who the narrator is. However, it’s highly unlikely nowadays that any reader coming to this chapter isn’t aware they’re reached the famous Molly Bloom monologue.
